items.title: Joey Morant interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013
items.q: I knew them too, very well.

ctx.x: I was in his hospital room every day to see him. And everybody thought he was black. See how people jump to assumption? They assumed he was black. They just assumed that, as if to say, oh somebody black got to do that. Not necessarily. He wrote all the hits.
Like Jerry Lieber and Mike Stoller.

There you go. I knew them too, very well. See? So there’s so much you can learn about life and man and his world, like “Desiderato.” I’ve got to mail him these. It’s a piece of prose written by an airline pilot, an unknown airline pilot, became a master to read. A masterpiece. “Desiderato.” You can pull it up, can’t you Linda? Linda: Oh yeah. © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-
